calls.reason: Anthropic's Amazon deal describes capacity still coming online through 2026, and OpenAI's AWS commitment includes Trainium4, which starts delivery in 2027. Amazon says data-center capital is spent years before revenue. Together these show the contracted capacity was not yet built.

The evidence is thin and mixed. Microsoft's roughly 1 point of AI contribution in 2023 says nothing about how revenue split between the labs and other customers, and a 3.6% drop in Microsoft's stock on one day cuts against the valuation story without settling it.

Whether the capex was well spent is a judgment, and no evidence matches AI returns against costs. Meta's conversion gains and Microsoft's quickly monetized capacity point the other way but do not settle returns.
This is a four-year forecast running to 2030. One beat of Microsoft's own guidance cannot test whether the labs will reach that revenue level or whether hyperscalers will miss expectations.

This is a conditional forecast whose condition has not happened. Anthropic's S-1 lists only a risk of failing to meet its compute obligations, and there is no evidence that either lab has actually been unable to pay.

Anthropic's audited S-1 reports a 2025 net loss of $42.0B, and reporting reviewed by the FT puts OpenAI's 2025 net loss near $39B. Both are unprofitable, though much of each loss is non-cash valuation charges.
